page: Microsoft Azure M416s_8_v2 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It is powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture, offering 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and features a massive memory footprint of 7600.0 GB, which equates to approximately 18.27 GB of RAM per core. It includes 4194 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25 percent. However, the massive core count drives top-tier multi-core performance in the top 10 percent for stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 20870.61 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 746.81 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10 percent. Conversely, Passmark memory score is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25 percent.

Given its massive memory capacity and high multi-core throughput, the M416s_8_v2 is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, and heavy data-processing workloads. This is supported by top-tier Redis SET operations at 307.64 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 113.81 GB/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a high-density consolidated resource profile. While single-threaded tasks and text-generation LLM inference are inefficient on this architecture, the server provides massive resource density for workloads that can fully parallelize across 416 vCPUs and utilize the 7.6 TB RAM.
